henry: Starting AegisCare POC perf sweep — mixed workload (generation + embeddings + rerank) to validate 99p targets for their triage assistant. Posting quick findings and proposed next steps.
lina: Nice — what's their target and what did the smoke show?
henry: Targets: sustained 900 qps mixed (approx 70% short-gen, 20% embedding lookups, 10% rerank), peaks to 3k qps for 45s. SLO ask: 99p gen < 375ms at sustained.
omar: numbers?
henry: Smoke 20m at 900 qps, seq_gen=48, seq_embed=256:
- Gen baseline (fp16) median 55ms, p95 125ms, p99 295ms.
- Gen quant (q5_0) median 46ms, p95 135ms, p99 intermittent spikes 750-1,100ms (~0.3% of requests).
- Embedding model (fp16) median 18ms, p95 45ms, p99 90ms.
- Rerank step adds median 12ms, but when ran concurrent with embedding-heavy bursts p99 for gen spikes.
lina: That's interesting — gen quant has better median but worse tail. Any idea why?
henry: Correlates with embedding cache flushes. Embedding requests use larger context windows and trigger larger KV writebacks on the host, evicting hot pages the gen path expects. We saw KV miss ratio jump from 2% -> 18% during the spikes.
ojulia: Can you paste exact bench commands you used?
henry: Sure — gen run:```
./bench --model redwood-2xl-v1 --variant q5_0 --seq 48 --qps 630 --concurrency 12 --prefetch async --ramp 300 --mix gen:0.7,embed:0.2,rerank:0.1
```
Embedding worker run (separate for profiling):```
./bench --model redwood-embed-v2 --variant fp16 --seq 256 --qps 270 --concurrency 8 --ramp 300 --prefetch true
```
henry: Burst test: 900 qps steady for 10m then a 45s storm at 3k qps. During the storm, quant gen p99 blew past 1s in a few windows while baseline stayed under 420ms.
omar: Hypothesis: shared KV/cache eviction + host memcpy stalls when embedding writes spike. Need metrics: gpu memcpy stalls, KV eviction histograms, nvlink saturation, and kernel queue depth.
lina: Agreed. Proposed mitigations: 1) partition KV caches per model group, 2) pin hot KV pages for gen path, 3) limit embedding writebacks during peak windows (throttle). Also consider routing embedding traffic to a separate pool.
ojulia: Can we reproduce quickly? ops-bot — any ded slot availability?
ops-bot: Candidate slot: ded-apac-12g reserved window available 2026-06-22 21:00-00:00 UTC. Please confirm if you want to book.
henry: Book it. Plan: run 3x 30m steady-state at 900 qps with synthetic prefix skew (60% hot, 40% unique) then 3x 45s peak storms. One run will enable KV partitioning, one will enable KV-pin, one will be baseline. Collect traces and perf counters.
omar: I'll instrument: nvlink bandwidth, gpu memcpy stalls, kernel evict logs, host page-fault histograms, and cgroup OOM/pressure. Also capture per-request KV hit/miss tags.
lina: Security/procurement asks from AegisCare: customer-managed KMS in their AWS account + HSM-backed signing, SAML SSO, and HIPAA/BAA. Any blockers?
compliance: Dedicated + Private supports customer KMS and AWS CloudHSM. We support HSM via PKCS11 in on-prem package for appliances. HIPAA/BAA: we can sign a BAA; need SOC2 docs and encryption-in-transit confirmation. No immediate blockers but need to validate SAML IdP details for SSO integration.
ojulia: Procurement wants a monthly uplift estimate for reserved 3k qps peak (10% headroom) vs PAYG to evaluate economics. Can we give a ballpark?
lina: Rough numbers: reserved burst commit (1yr, multi-AZ SLA) ~ $33k/month uplift. PAYG estimate for the same capacity profile ~ $58k/month. If we can validate gen quant stability (reduce p99 by ~65%) we can offer token-cost savings estimate ~16% on their projected mix.
omar: Also recommend setting up a canary fallback route: default to quant gen, but automatically fallback to baseline model for requests hitting tail latency thresholds (e.g., >300ms) to keep user experience consistent while we iterate on runtime.
henry: Good call. I'll add a 7% canary fallback to baseline and an experiment that toggles KV partitioning.
compliance: I'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs to the shared folder and start BAA intake with legal. Also confirm CloudHSM vendor compatibility if they have a preferred vendor.
ojulia: Next actions:
- henry/omar: run 3x30m steady + 3x45s storms during ded-apac-12g slot with runs: baseline, KV-partition, KV-pin (target: 2026-06-22 slot)
- omar: collect nvlink/gpu memcpy, kernel eviction, host page-fault histograms, cgroup logs, per-request KV tags
- lina: send procurement ballpark and ask for their target go-live quarter by EOW
- compliance: post SOC2/ISO links and start BAA intake; confirm HSM vendor checklist
- henry: add canary fallback config to the POC doc and link routes
- ops-bot: confirm slot booking and allocate ded-apac-12g slot for the run

henry: If we can get gen 99p < 375ms at 900 qps on Dedicated with fallback, sales will push for a 12-mo committed arrangement. Let's keep traces clean and tag runs clearly.
ops-bot: Slot booked: ded-apac-12g, 2026-06-22 21:00-00:00 UTC.
lina: I'll compile a short A/B cost matrix (baseline vs q5 quant vs mixed) and drop in the shared sales folder after runs.
omar: I'll open a runtime ticket for KV partitioning + pinning and link results here once PRs are ready.
henry: Thanks all. Will post raw CSVs, flamegraphs, and a short run writeup in this thread after the window. :hammer_and_wrench:
